question_text: Draw an RC Low-Pass filter. Explain how to construct its Bode plot and describe the rule for its slope.
answer_text: A resistor in series, with a capacitor to ground.
explanation_text:
Bode plots are drawn based on the order (number of reactive components) of the filter. A 1st-order filter (like this one RC circuit) changes at exactly ±20 dB/decade.

Magnitude Plot: It starts perfectly flat at 0 dB (a gain of 1) because low frequencies pass freely through the resistor. At the cutoff frequency (f_c = 1 / 2πRC), the capacitor's impedance drops to equal the resistor, cutting the signal power in half (-3 dB point). Beyond f_c, the capacitor's impedance continues to drop, shorting the signal to ground. Since it is 1st-order, the plot rolls off linearly downward at -20 dB per decade.
Phase Plot: Starts at 0°, hits -45° exactly at f_c, and maxes out at -90° at high frequencies.
bonus_question_text: What happens to the cutoff frequency if you double both the resistor and capacitor values?
bonus_answer_text: The cutoff frequency decreases by a factor of 4 (it becomes 25% of the original frequency).
